title: The Harvard Science Research Mentoring Program
extended_summary:
This paper describes the founding, design, and first two years of operation of the Harvard Science Research Mentoring Program (SRMP), a year-long mentoring program intended to give high-school students authentic research experiences in astrophysics while also providing graduate students and postdoctoral scholars with mentoring experience. The author frames SRMP as a response to gaps in STEM mentoring and the need for role models, research exposure, and advisor-training opportunities that are often not provided in graduate education.

The intervention is not a controlled instructional study but a program model: students are recruited from Cambridge Rindge and Latin School, selected through essays and interviews, then paired with mentors for September-to-May independent research projects. The program includes an orientation, introductory astrophysics sessions, twice-weekly student-mentor meetings, monthly cohort meetings, and an end-of-year symposium. Mentors are primarily advanced graduate students and postdocs, and the author emphasizes flexible, hands-on or hands-off supervision depending on the project and student needs.

The paper reports descriptive implementation details and testimonials from students and mentors, along with limited survey-based evaluation. The main conclusions are that the program appears to support student engagement, coding and research skill development, and professional identity exploration, while also benefiting mentors’ professional development as novice advisors. The author argues that the long timescale and authentic research context are important features of SRMP and that the model could be replicated at other institutions.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a descriptive/programmatic paper about a science research mentoring program, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tutoring, coaching, or feedback system. No controlled or quasi-controlled analysis of an AI tool is reported.
